newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt ends a touch wider, key U.S. data eyed.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt ends a touch wider, key U.S. data eyed.

text.p: Brady bond prices ended a touch wider lagging U.S. Treasuries, as market participants focused on upcoming key U.S. economic data, emerging market traders said.
Spreads were seen wider across the board by about two basis points; however, Mexico debt widened between two to nine basis points, traders said.
"It was a pretty neutral day overall; however, I'm somewhat surprised that spreads did not tighten with the strong move in Treasuries today," said one Brady trader.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed up 13/32 at 104-11/32 to yield 6.30 percent, its lowest level since mid-February, 1996.

"This probably reflects two things -- one that, generally people are long here -- and two that, people are skittish to aggressively buy at these levels, in front of tomorrow's key payrolls report," the trader said.
The U.S. Labor Department will release July figures for payroll/unemployment at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict an increase in payrolls of 193,000 versus a gain of 127,000 in June. The unemployment rate is expected to dip to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent in the prior month.
"Customer flow was pretty limited today, with the bias to the sell-side," said another Brady trader. "I think people were pretty much already positioned going into the numbers."
"If we see a number that's bullish for the market players will come back in," he added.
Meanwhile, among Brady issues, Mexican global bonds were quoted two basis points wider, discounts widened by seven basis points, and par bonds traded wider by about nine basis points, traders said.
"We saw some selling overnight in Tokyo ... so we opened softer," said one Brady player. "The selling we did see today was predominately in Mexico."
Mexico Discounts were quoted off 1/4 at 94-5/8 bid.
Among other latin credits, Argentine Pars gained 1/2 to 75-7/8 bid, Frbs gained 1/4 to 95-1/4 bid. Brazil C bonds rose 1/4 to 84-1/2 bid.
Turning to eastern European credits, Russian VN US$ rose 1/8 to 95-1/8 bid. Bulgaria Flirbs rose 1/8 to 62-1/2, IAB's gained 3/8 to 77-1/2 bid.
In credit specific news, Merrill Lynch & Co fixed income strategist, Andrew Kenningham said Bulgaria's creditworthiness has improved dramatically in the past six months and is currently out of date.

In a press release, Kenningham said, major U.S. credit rating agencies are likely to award Bulgaria, who currently holds the lowest credit rating of any sovereign borrower at B3, a B1 rating by early 1998.
The strategist added that if current favorable economic and political trends continue Bulgaria could conceivably be upgraded to a low BB range by 1999.

In country specific news, U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday that the United States was watching recent developments in Asian emerging markets closely and welcomed ongoing discussions between the International Monetary Fund and Thailand.
The IMF is holding talks with Thai officials this week on an austerity package to help the country overcome its worse economic crisis in more than a decade.
Summers cautioned, however, not to underestimate the long-term impact of current currency volatility.
